intro: Laténa, the commune at the northern end of Lake Neuchâtel, officially La Tène, the name given to a whole period of Celtic Europe, has one place on our map: the park of the Préfargier estate at Marin-Epagnier. A reader walked through it and photographed five trees, three Atlas cedars grown into one crown, a tall cedar on the lawn, a dawn redwood, three weeping beeches and a large-leaved lime.
meta_description: Three Atlas cedars at Préfargier in Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel: a reader's photograph, where they stand and how to see them.

trees.name: The Three Atlas Cedars of Préfargier

location.address: Parc du domaine de Préfargier, Marin-Epagnier, Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel

trees.story:
Three Atlas cedars stand together on one lawn in the park of the Préfargier estate, in the commune of Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel. A reader sent us their photograph and put it in one line, “3 cèdres de l’Atlas, dans le park du domaine de la maison de santé de Préfargier.”

The photograph shows why it was worth a picture. Three separate trunks rise a few metres apart and their crowns have grown into a single dark, broad pyramid, with silvery blue-green needles at the branch tips, the colour the Atlas cedar, Cedrus atlantica, is known for. It comes from the Atlas Mountains of Morocco and Algeria. A bench stands under the nearest trunk, and a walker on the gravel path beside the lawn looks small next to the whole.

Each trunk is broad and dark, and the lowest limbs sweep out over the grass almost to the ground, so the group spreads far across the lawn. In the photograph the light is grey, an autumn day, and the cedars are the darkest thing in the park, against the yellowing woods behind them.

The reader who sent the photograph went back with a tape. By their measure the trunks are around 4.23 metres round, taken a metre above the ground. We have found no height or planting date for the three, so this page gives none.

Walk to the edge of the lawn and the three crowns read as one tree.
trees.how_to_recognise: Three Atlas cedars on one open lawn beside a gravel path, their crowns joined into one broad pyramid of blue-green needles, with a bench under the nearest trunk.
trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-05: published from a reader's app photograph, note and GPS fix (sighting 15a3b6f1) on Hidde's 2026-10-21 ruling that a good photograph with a GPS fix is not held. Species, location and the grouping of three are the reader's, and the photograph shows three conifers with glaucous blue-green foliage and horizontal tiered branches, consistent with Atlas cedar. No register entry within 100 m and no encyclopaedia article within 300 m; two web searches found no source on the park. Access: the estate is a health-care site (maison de santé), no source states its opening hours, but the cedars stand beside a gravel footpath with a walker on it in the photograph, so the tree is clearly seen from public ground (rule 10); access says so plainly. No girth, height or age.
trees.access: Seen from a gravel footpath along the lawn in the estate's park, where walkers pass. We found no opening hours for the grounds, so respect any signs at the entrance.

trees.name: The Tall Cedar of Préfargier

location.address: Parc du domaine de Préfargier, Marin-Epagnier, Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel

trees.story:
A tall cedar stands on the lawn of the Préfargier park in Laténa, and a reader measured its girth at 705 centimetres. They photographed it twice, once from a distance and once close to the trunk.

The photograph shows one straight trunk, silvery blue-green needles in tufts along layered, level limbs and a crown that narrows toward the top, which is how an Atlas cedar looks. The reader called it a giant sequoia, but the frame does not show one, so we list it as a cedar and the species is open to correction. We have found no register entry, planting date or height for it, so the girth is the reader's figure. Seven metres round would be a large trunk for a tree in a European park.

It stands in the same park as the Three Atlas Cedars of Préfargier, a short walk across the lawns. Tell us what you find if you put a tape round it. If you can confirm the species, or give a height or a planting date, the page will take it.

trees.name: The Dawn Redwood of Préfargier

location.address: Parc du domaine de Préfargier, Marin-Epagnier, Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel

trees.story:
A dawn redwood stands on a lawn of the Préfargier park in Laténa, and a reader photographed it in its autumn colour, the whole crown burnt orange against a pale blue sky. They named it a métaséquoia, the French name for Metasequoia, and gave a girth of 250 centimetres.

The photograph shows a straight trunk with ivy climbing it, a broad crown of fine feathery leaves and a dark evergreen conifer behind it that makes the colour stand out. A gravel path runs along the bottom of the frame. The dawn redwood sheds its needles each year, which is unusual for a conifer, and the orange phase lasts only a few weeks.

We found no register entry or planting date, so the girth is the reader's figure. The tree stands in the same park as the Three Atlas Cedars of Préfargier. If you can give a height or a planting date for it, the page will take that too.

trees.name: The Weeping Beeches of Préfargier

location.address: Parc du domaine de Préfargier, Marin-Epagnier, Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel

trees.story:
Three weeping beeches grow together on a lawn of the Préfargier park in Laténa, and their drooping branches have joined into one huge curtain of leaves that reaches almost to the ground. A reader photographed them in autumn with the single note “3 hêtres pleureurs”, three weeping beeches.

In the photograph the mass of leaves is many times the height of the visitor who stands under its edge, green with yellow and gold at the tips. Behind it the other trees are in orange autumn colour.

We found no register entry, girth or planting date, so this page gives none. A weeping beech is a cultivated form of the common beech, grown for its hanging shoots, and it grows into just this kind of tent.

It stands in the same park as the Three Atlas Cedars of Préfargier. If you know how old they are, or how many trunks there are under the curtain, the page will take that too.

trees.name: The Large-leaved Lime of Préfargier

location.address: Parc du domaine de Préfargier, Marin-Epagnier, Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel

trees.story:
A large-leaved lime stands near the wall of the Préfargier park in Laténa, and a reader photographed it in late autumn when its leaves had turned yellow-green. They named the species and gave no measurements.

The crown is a wide, even dome, so full that it hides most of its own branches, and many slender stems rise straight up from the main limbs as if the tree had been cut back to a stool long ago. Ivy climbs the trunk. Behind it stands an old garden wall with a small brick fountain niche, and to the right the shuttered pale walls of a house.

We found no register entry, girth or planting date for the tree, so this page gives none. It makes a handsome pair of landmarks with the cedars of the same park.

If you have a tape, a girth would be welcome here, and so would a planting date from anyone who knows the estate's history.

question_meta: Three Atlas cedars grow together at Préfargier, Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel. Where they stand and how to see them.
question_answer: A reader found five remarkable trees in the park of the Préfargier estate at Marin-Epagnier, in Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel: three Atlas cedars growing together, a tall cedar, a dawn redwood, three weeping beeches and a large-leaved lime.
question_context: Everything this page says about the cedars comes from one reader's photograph and note, sent through the app on 5 November 2026. No tree register we hold lists them, we found no published survey of the Préfargier park that names them, and we have no girth, height or planting date. The photograph is the evidence. It shows three separate trunks a few metres apart on an open lawn, low limbs that sweep almost to the grass, and blue-green needles held in flat tiers, the look of the Atlas cedar, Cedrus atlantica, a conifer from the Atlas Mountains of Morocco and Algeria that is often grown in European parks. Together the three read as one broad dark pyramid against the woods behind. The park belongs to a health-care institution, the maison de santé de Préfargier, and we found no published opening hours for its grounds. The cedars stand beside a gravel footpath, and the reader's photograph shows another walker on it. If you know when they were planted, or have put a tape round one of the trunks, tell us on the page and it goes into this answer.

faq.q: What kind of trees are they?
faq.a: Atlas cedars, a tall cedar, a dawn redwood, weeping beeches and a large-leaved lime.
In the park of the Préfargier estate, Marin-Epagnier, in the commune of Laténa, canton of Neuchâtel.
We have found no planting date or measurement for them except a reader's girths for the tall cedar and the dawn redwood.
